title: mirotalksfu
same: Every counted sample's results were read from its own job logs. In all 20 counted samples (5 per configuration, cold, and 5 per configuration, warm) the same 2 jobs ran and passed: `test`, the project's mocha tests (every sample's mocha total passed with no failures; 851 passing in the logs checked by hand), and `build`, which built the Docker image for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The image build is checked by its steps completing (the mediasoup worker, the dependency install and the three application layers for each CPU type; a cached step counts as complete), not by comparing images byte for byte. The image is built but not published.
notes: **Control configuration.** Each round also replayed the event on StarSling runners with the CI unchanged, as an internal control. It is not part of this comparison, and its samples are not shown on this page.

**Lane: merges to the default branch.** This page measures merges to mirotalksfu's default branch. The default branch is `main`. Each sample replays the merge of `e76e48f6`. PR updates were not measured: upstream's only workflow runs on merges to the default branch and has no pull-request trigger.

**Workflows in this merge.** The replayed merge runs upstream's only workflow, `ci.yml`: the tests, then one `build` job that builds the image for both CPU types under emulation (QEMU) in a single job.

**One repository per lane.** Most samples ran concurrently, each in its own repository (one repository per lane: `benchmark-mirotalksfu-lane1` to `benchmark-mirotalksfu-lane6`, with the same branches, events and payloads as this repository), so their caches never mix; a cold sample ran with no caches in its repository. 8 of the 20 samples on this page (cold rounds 1 to 4, both configurations) came from an earlier sequential run of the same configuration in this repository, one sample at a time; the other 12 came from the lanes.

**Root and non-root StarSling samples, pooled.** At about 11:13 AM PST on 2026-11-16, StarSling switched this organization's jobs from root to an ordinary (non-root) user. Of the 10 StarSling Runners (with agents) samples, 3 ran as root (cold rounds 1 to 3) and 7 as non-root. The owner accepted mixing them. Before pooling, the agent PR's step (`Build & Push`) was compared across the two: cold, one non-root sample was about 1.6% slower than the slowest root sample (1,623 s against 1,597 s), and the other (1,585 s) fell inside the root range. That is inside the run-to-run spread, so the samples are pooled.

**Disk-storage voids, re-run.** This benchmark counts StarSling samples only when the runner had its usual RAM disk. One control sample (cold round 3) ran on runners whose RAM disk could not be confirmed after a storage change in this organization; it was voided and re-run once, and the re-run fills its slot. Neither run is on this page or in any number on it. No GitHub-hosted or StarSling Runners (with agents) sample was voided.

**Collector fix.** The test collector that reads each job log was fixed during the benchmark: when the app printed console output around a mocha suite header (first seen with the `PresenterManager` suite), it did not start the new suite. The record this page uses was built with the fixed collector. In one GitHub-hosted sample (warm round 2) a log line printed right after the `RemoteControlSetup` header, so that suite's tests are listed under the previous suite; the sample's mocha total passed, with 851 passing as in the others.

**Bench-only changes, identical in every configuration and never part of the agent PR:**
  - Switched off: the Docker Hub login and the image push (`push: false`; the image is still built for both CPUs, then discarded). Upstream has no guard on either. The Docker Hub secrets do not exist here and nothing may be published; upstream did run the login and push on this merge, so that work is not in any column. The two secret references are removed.
  - Time limit: the benchmark waits up to 150 minutes for a sample (the default is 60; upstream's own `build` job took 69 minutes). This is a wait limit only; nothing measured changes.
  - One harness step, `Benchmark event context (harness)`, is added at the start of every job. It prints two IDs so each job can be matched to its sample; its median time is 0 s.
  - Different Ubuntu image on StarSling: upstream runs Ubuntu 22.04. StarSling has no 22.04 runner, so StarSling runs `starsling-ubuntu-24.04` while GitHub runs `ubuntu-22.04-4core`. The Docker image is built inside containers, so the host image affects only the Docker and QEMU setup.
  - Warm seed: warm samples start from a cache a seed run left behind, produced by replaying the previous upstream merge (`46231380`) on the same configuration; its time is not counted. mediasoup is at the same version (3.32.2) in the seed and in the replayed merge, so the worker layer is reusable.
  - On the agent PR's own branch only, never in a replay: a setup commit points the workflow's trigger at that branch and the runners at StarSling, and applies the same login and push switch-off, so the PR's checks run there.

**Runner sizes.** Upstream's `ubuntu-22.04` jobs run on GitHub `ubuntu-22.04-4core` (4 vCPU, 16 GiB) and StarSling `starsling-ubuntu-24.04` (4 vCPU, 16 GiB). StarSling's 4 vCPU runners can burst to 5 vCPU and 32 GB RAM (Afterburner); GitHub's 4-core runners have 16 GB. Both jobs run on these labels. The linux/arm64 image is built under QEMU emulation on these x64 runners in every configuration, as upstream does.

**Upstream reference (context only; not like-for-like; not the headline).** What upstream sees today, on upstream's own GitHub runners over the last 60 days (315 successful runs), counted separately. Uncached (the Docker worker layer is rebuilt): a median 102.3 min per merge to the default branch (n=283; last 10 median 83.3 min). Cached (the layer cache hits): a median 1.7 min (n=32), a different kind of run. Standard runners, many commits; not a like-for-like replay.

agentPrs.summary: Build the mediasoup C++ worker in its own Docker stage, keyed on the mediasoup version in `package-lock.json`, so changes to the app or to other dependencies no longer rebuild it. One file, `Dockerfile`: a stage reads the mediasoup version, a second stage builds the worker (cached by that version), `npm ci` skips the worker build, and the built worker is copied in. The npm cache mount also gets one id per CPU type, because the two image builds now run `npm ci` at the same time; that part is for safety and changes no timing.

whatWasSlow: Every merge to mirotalksfu's default branch runs one workflow, `ci.yml`: the tests (a median 28 s on GitHub-hosted runners, cold), then one `build` job that builds the Docker image for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. That one job is almost the whole wait: cold, `build` took a median 6,064 s of the 6,098 s merge on GitHub-hosted runners (warm, 5,129 s of 5,171 s). The image build compiles the mediasoup C++ worker from source inside the Dockerfile, once per CPU type, and the arm64 copy runs under CPU emulation (QEMU), where that compile is very slow. Without the fix it reruns whenever the Dockerfile's dependency step reruns, which is for any change to the dependencies or the app version, so warm caches barely help.
whatWeChanged:
The original showcase for this project proposed one fix: build the worker in its own cached stage. We measured it on StarSling, with 5 runs on each side (the CI as it was, and the CI with the fix), on the step it changes. Cold means no caches at the start; warm means starting from the cache a seed run left behind.

| Fix | Result | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Build the mediasoup worker in its own stage, cached by the mediasoup version (with a per-CPU npm cache id) | `Build & Push` step of the `build` job, warm: 1,507 s to 77 s (median), **19.6x faster**; every run with the fix beat every run without it. Cold: 1,636 s to 1,586 s (median), about 3% faster, and the runs overlap: with nothing cached, the arm64 worker still compiles under QEMU. | Kept (agent PR 1) |

The fix is a cache, so it only helps when an earlier merge has built the worker at the same mediasoup version. A merge that changes the mediasoup version rebuilds the worker even with the fix, and then looks like a cold run. The full benchmark runs both cold and warm, over 5 rounds each.
